subject.title: Los Alamitos — Measure G (Los Alamitos Hotel Tax (TOT Measure))

text: Shall the ordinance providing funding for City of Los Alamitos’ general services such as maintaining 911 emergency response and police services; providing neighborhood police patrols; maintaining parks; supporting youth, afterschool, and senior programs; repairing streets and potholes; by increasing the City of Los Alamitos’ transient occupancy tax, paid only by hotel/motel and short-term rental guests, from 8% to 12%, providing approximately $300,000 annually be adopted?
A “yes” vote on Measure G is a vote to increase the TOT tax rate from 8% to 12%.
A “no” vote on Measure G is a vote to maintain the current TOT tax rate at 8%.

analysis.title: Impartial Analysis

text: The City of Los Alamitos (“City”) currently imposes a transient occupancy tax (“TOT”), also generally known as a “hotel” tax, at the rate of eight percent (8%) of rent paid by guests to occupy a hotel room or similar lodging. The TOT is imposed upon occupancy of a hotel room or similar lodging within the City for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days or less. The TOT currently provides approximately $600,000.00 annually to the General Fund to pay for general City services and programs.

Measure G was placed on the ballot by the Los Alamitos City Council and, if approved by a majority of Los Alamitos voters, will amend the Los Alamitos Municipal Code to increase the TOT tax rate from eight percent (8%) to twelve percent (12%) of the rent paid by guests to occupy a hotel room or similar lodging. It is anticipated that this rate increase will generate an additional $300,000.00 in new revenues.

Measure G would be a “general tax”. All revenue from this tax would be deposited into the City’s General Fund and could be used for general City operations and services, including public safety, infrastructure maintenance, park and facility improvements, and other community priorities identified by residents and the City Council. Pursuant to State Law, a “general tax” requires approval by a majority of the City’s voters voting at an election.
A “yes” vote on Measure G is a vote to increase the TOT tax rate from 8% to 12%.
A “no” vote on Measure G is a vote to maintain the current TOT tax rate at 8%.

text: VOTE YES ON MEASURE G, LOS ALAMITOS HOTEL TAX (TOT MEASURE) MEASURE

People live in Los Alamitos because it offers an exceptional quality of life and great local services while maintaining fiscal responsibility. Measure G is a practical, locally controlled solution that will help protect essential city services without increasing taxes on residents.

Measure G increases the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) paid by hotel, motel, and short-term rental guests from 8% to 12%. This tax is paid by visitors staying in Los Alamitos, not by local residents. Even with this adjustment, Los Alamitos’ hotel tax rate will remain competitive with neighboring cities.
If approved, Measure G is expected to generate approximately $300,000 annually to support community priorities, including:
Maintaining 911 emergency response and police services
Providing neighborhood police patrols and public safety programs
Maintaining parks and community facilities
Supporting youth, afterschool, and senior programs
Repairing streets, potholes, and other critical infrastructure

Additionally, our city will see an increase in tourism as Olympic sporting events take place in neighboring communities. These visitors bring increased traffic and demand on Los Alamitos’ city services, including streets, emergency medical services, and police protection. However, the cost of providing those services to visitors disproportionately falls on our local taxpayers.

As costs continue to rise, Measure G provides a reliable source of local funding that cannot be taken by the State and remains under local control. Every dollar generated will stay in Los Alamitos and be used to support services that directly benefit our community.

This measure helps ensure that visitors contribute their fair share toward the services and infrastructure they use while visiting our city. It is a sensible approach that strengthens public safety, preserves quality of life, and invests in the future of Los Alamitos.
Vote
on Measure G.
